- **Two new dispatch phases, `Retrieve` and `WaitRetrieve`, ahead of everything else** (`Adapters/DispatchService.cs`), so the order is now Retrieve â†’ ARC â†’ GBR â†’ Artisan. Per material: ask Artisan what it can actually see on the retainers, start the withdrawal, wait for its task queue to drain, then **measure the bag-count delta** â€” Artisan going idle is not proof anything moved, the same lesson as `WaitCraftEnd` in 0.1.1.0. A partial pull is expected, because `RestockFromRetainers` stops as soon as one retainer's pass satisfies its own bag check, so the remainder is re-queued, bounded at 4 attempts per item. A 4-minute watchdog aborts a stuck session and reports why.
- **Post-fetch re-plan** (`DispatchService.AfterRetrieve`) â€” once anything has actually landed in the bags, the cart is re-planned against the new inventory, so crafts that were deferred purely because their materials sat on a retainer become real crafts. This is the difference between `crafts finished 0/0, 4 still to retrieve` and `crafts finished 107/107`. Deferrals caused by a retrieval we are about to perform are no longer printed up front â€” the player is not told a craft is blocked and then told it ran; whatever is still stuck after the fetch is reported once, at the end.
- `DispatchService.RetrieveOne(itemId, quantity)` and `DispatchService.RetrieveOnly(retrievals)` â€” the fetch machinery without the crafting, for the tree button and `/lcraft fetch`.
- `Configuration.cs` â€” `RetrieveFromRetainers` (config v4), **ON by default**: an existing config that never had the field gets the new behaviour, because that is the fix that was asked for. It is opt-out, not opt-in.
- `UI/SettingsTab.cs` â€” checkbox "Fetch missing materials from your retainers before crafting (needs a summoning bell)" with a help marker naming the requirements, plus `RetainerFetch.Pin` in the reflection-pin health list.
- `UI/IngredientTree.cs` â€” a **Retrieve** button on any leaf whose stock is owned but outside the bags, plus a `Places()` helper for its tooltip. It sits before the `leaf.Missing == 0` early-out on purpose: a leaf can be fully "have" and still be unreachable, which is exactly the case the old UI had no button for.
- `Plugin.cs` â€” `/lcraft fetch`: retrieve the cart's out-of-bags materials and stop there. `/lcraft guard` now also lists and verifies the Artisan retainer-fetch pin.
- `tests/LazyCrafter.Harness/RetrieveTests.cs` (new, 8 cases; harness now **111/111**, was 103) â€” the decision logic around the fetch: a regression case that reproduces the 0.1.1.0 nag loop (same cart, same inventory, replanned twice â†’ identical refusal both times), the post-fetch re-plan turning a deferral into a craft, partial-pull remainder arithmetic, the execution-time guard clearing once stock lands, saddlebag stock still being named rather than promised, and Joey's actual cart shape at 107 runs ending in one Artisan craft of 107 rather than four retrieve lines.
- `tests/LazyCrafter.GuardProbe/` â€” `RetainerFetch.Pin` is verified offline against the installed Artisan DLL alongside GBR and ARC (its csproj now compiles `RetainerFetch.cs`), including the simulated version-mismatch and renamed-member paths.


- `Adapters/DispatchService.cs` (`Finish`) â€” the summary carries `retrieved M/N` and, when applicable, `, K could not be retrieved`; both are measured from bag deltas rather than from a success return.
- `Adapters/DispatchService.cs` (`Stop`) â€” also aborts Artisan's retainer task queue when stopped mid-fetch.


- **Why this drives Artisan and not AutoRetainer, despite AutoRetainer being the card's first choice.** Read from the installed `AutoRetainer.dll` 4.6.1.34 with ILSpy 11.0.0.9375 â€” decompiled, not guessed from the string table. Its 27 IPC names are all venture / postprocess / multi-mode and none withdraws an item. The only reverse-direction code it has is `AutoRetainer.Scheduler.Tasks.TaskEntrustDuplicates.EnqueueNewReverse(EntrustPlan)`, public static, and it is the wrong shape three times over. (1) Its first queued step is literally *"Wait until addon SelectString ready"*: it assumes a retainer session is **already open**, and contains no bell interaction and no retainer selection, so it cannot start from a standing player. (2) It is driven by an `EntrustPlan` whose `EntrustItemsAmountToKeep` is an amount-to-keep-at-the-far-end, not an amount-to-fetch, and it moves whole slots via `MoveSlotFromToRetainerInventoryUnsafe` rather than a requested quantity. (3) `RetrieveFromRetainer` â€” the promising-looking name in the string table â€” is a literal of the `RetainerItemCommand` enum, not a callable. So the card's stated fallback applies, and Artisan's restock does the entire job including the bell.
- **`howManyToGet` has two meanings inside Artisan**, verified in the decompiled body: a *delta* inside `ExtractSingular` (`value = Min(howManyToGet, foundInThisStack)`, then `howManyToGet -= value`) but an *absolute bag target* in the per-retainer abort check (`NumberOfIngredient(item) >= howManyToGet`). Passing the delta withdraws the delta and then stops, which is what we want, but it can also stop early after a partial pull â€” hence the measure-and-return loop rather than trusting the call.
- **A summoning bell is required, and only retainers are reachable.** The chocobo saddlebag, the armoury chest and the glamour dresser are not bell inventories, so stock sitting there is still named and refused â€” once, with the reason â€” rather than silently retried. Same for AllaganTools being absent (Artisan's retainer features are a no-op without it) and for the toggle being off. Every refusal now says what to do about it instead of repeating itself.
- The guard-style refusal from 0.1.1.0 is untouched and still the safety net: a craft whose materials are not in the bags at the instant of hand-off is never sent to Artisan.

v0.1.2.0 (2026-09-03)



- **Retainer withdrawal, by reflection into Artisan 4.0.5.19** â€” new `Adapters/Dispatch/RetainerFetch.cs`, behind `ReflectionGuard` with a version pin of `[4.0.5, 4.1)` and 10 pinned members. It wraps `Artisan.IPC.RetainerInfo.RestockFromRetainers(uint itemId, int howManyToGet)` (public static), which enqueues the whole session on Artisan's own `TaskManager`: lock YesAlready, target and interact with the nearest summoning bell, then per retainer holding the item â€” select it, "Entrust Items", open the item's context menu, type the quantity into `InputNumeric`, close, quit â€” aborting as soon as the bags hold enough. It suppresses AutoRetainer for the duration (`AutoRetainer.SetSuppressed`), so the two do not fight over the bell. Also exposes `Blocker()` (a one-sentence, actionable reason a fetch cannot run: AllaganTools off, no bell in range, already busy), `Available(itemId)` (refreshes Artisan's `RetainerData` via `GetRetainerItemCount(id, tryCache:false)` â€” which is also what makes `RestockFromRetainers` able to do anything, since it returns immediately when that cache has no entry for the item), `Busy()` and `Abort()`.
- **Two new dispatch phases, `Retrieve` and `WaitRetrieve`, ahead of everything else** (`Adapters/DispatchService.cs`), so the order is now Retrieve â†’ ARC â†’ GBR â†’ Artisan. Per material: ask Artisan what it can actually see on the retainers, start the withdrawal, wait for its task queue to drain, then **measure the bag-count delta** â€” Artisan going idle is not proof anything moved, the same lesson as `WaitCraftEnd` in 0.1.1.0. A partial pull is expected, because `RestockFromRetainers` stops as soon as one retainer's pass satisfies its own bag check, so the remainder is re-queued, bounded at 4 attempts per item. A 4-minute watchdog aborts a stuck session and reports why.
- **Post-fetch re-plan** (`DispatchService.AfterRetrieve`) â€” once anything has actually landed in the bags, the cart is re-planned against the new inventory, so crafts that were deferred purely because their materials sat on a retainer become real crafts. This is the difference between `crafts finished 0/0, 4 still to retrieve` and `crafts finished 107/107`. Deferrals caused by a retrieval we are about to perform are no longer printed up front â€” the player is not told a craft is blocked and then told it ran; whatever is still stuck after the fetch is reported once, at the end.
- `DispatchService.RetrieveOne(itemId, quantity)` and `DispatchService.RetrieveOnly(retrievals)` â€” the fetch machinery without the crafting, for the tree button and `/lcraft fetch`.
- `Configuration.cs` â€” `RetrieveFromRetainers` (config v4), **ON by default**: an existing config that never had the field gets the new behaviour, because that is the fix that was asked for. It is opt-out, not opt-in.
- `UI/SettingsTab.cs` â€” checkbox "Fetch missing materials from your retainers before crafting (needs a summoning bell)" with a help marker naming the requirements, plus `RetainerFetch.Pin` in the reflection-pin health list.
- `UI/IngredientTree.cs` â€” a **Retrieve** button on any leaf whose stock is owned but outside the bags, plus a `Places()` helper for its tooltip. It sits before the `leaf.Missing == 0` early-out on purpose: a leaf can be fully "have" and still be unreachable, which is exactly the case the old UI had no button for.
- `Plugin.cs` â€” `/lcraft fetch`: retrieve the cart's out-of-bags materials and stop there. `/lcraft guard` now also lists and verifies the Artisan retainer-fetch pin.
- `tests/LazyCrafter.Harness/RetrieveTests.cs` (new, 8 cases; harness now **111/111**, was 103) â€” the decision logic around the fetch: a regression case that reproduces the 0.1.1.0 nag loop (same cart, same inventory, replanned twice â†’ identical refusal both times), the post-fetch re-plan turning a deferral into a craft, partial-pull remainder arithmetic, the execution-time guard clearing once stock lands, saddlebag stock still being named rather than promised, and Joey's actual cart shape at 107 runs ending in one Artisan craft of 107 rather than four retrieve lines.
- `tests/LazyCrafter.GuardProbe/` â€” `RetainerFetch.Pin` is verified offline against the installed Artisan DLL alongside GBR and ARC (its csproj now compiles `RetainerFetch.cs`), including the simulated version-mismatch and renamed-member paths.


- `Adapters/DispatchService.cs` (`Finish`) â€” the summary carries `retrieved M/N` and, when applicable, `, K could not be retrieved`; both are measured from bag deltas rather than from a success return.
- `Adapters/DispatchService.cs` (`Stop`) â€” also aborts Artisan's retainer task queue when stopped mid-fetch.


- **Why this drives Artisan and not AutoRetainer, despite AutoRetainer being the card's first choice.** Read from the installed `AutoRetainer.dll` 4.6.1.34 with ILSpy 11.0.0.9375 â€” decompiled, not guessed from the string table. Its 27 IPC names are all venture / postprocess / multi-mode and none withdraws an item. The only reverse-direction code it has is `AutoRetainer.Scheduler.Tasks.TaskEntrustDuplicates.EnqueueNewReverse(EntrustPlan)`, public static, and it is the wrong shape three times over. (1) Its first queued step is literally *"Wait until addon SelectString ready"*: it assumes a retainer session is **already open**, and contains no bell interaction and no retainer selection, so it cannot start from a standing player. (2) It is driven by an `EntrustPlan` whose `EntrustItemsAmountToKeep` is an amount-to-keep-at-the-far-end, not an amount-to-fetch, and it moves whole slots via `MoveSlotFromToRetainerInventoryUnsafe` rather than a requested quantity. (3) `RetrieveFromRetainer` â€” the promising-looking name in the string table â€” is a literal of the `RetainerItemCommand` enum, not a callable. So the card's stated fallback applies, and Artisan's restock does the entire job including the bell.
- **`howManyToGet` has two meanings inside Artisan**, verified in the decompiled body: a *delta* inside `ExtractSingular` (`value = Min(howManyToGet, foundInThisStack)`, then `howManyToGet -= value`) but an *absolute bag target* in the per-retainer abort check (`NumberOfIngredient(item) >= howManyToGet`). Passing the delta withdraws the delta and then stops, which is what we want, but it can also stop early after a partial pull â€” hence the measure-and-return loop rather than trusting the call.
- **A summoning bell is required, and only retainers are reachable.** The chocobo saddlebag, the armoury chest and the glamour dresser are not bell inventories, so stock sitting there is still named and refused â€” once, with the reason â€” rather than silently retried. Same for AllaganTools being absent (Artisan's retainer features are a no-op without it) and for the toggle being off. Every refusal now says what to do about it instead of repeating itself.
- The guard-style refusal from 0.1.1.0 is untouched and still the safety net: a craft whose materials are not in the bags at the instant of hand-off is never sent to Artisan.
- Bullets in this entry are deliberately unwrapped single lines. `tools/Package-Plugin.ps1`'s CHANGELOG parser only keeps lines starting with `-`, `**` or a digit, so a hard-wrapped bullet loses everything after its first line in the user-facing `Changelog` field (visible in older entries above).

- **Retainer withdrawal, by reflection into Artisan 4.0.5.19** â€” new `Adapters/Dispatch/RetainerFetch.cs`, behind `ReflectionGuard` with a version pin of `[4.0.5, 4.1)` and 10 pinned members. It wraps `Artisan.IPC.RetainerInfo.RestockFromRetainers(uint itemId, int howManyToGet)` (public static), which enqueues the whole session on Artisan's own `TaskManager`: lock YesAlready, target and interact with the nearest summoning bell, then per retainer holding the item â€” select it, "Entrust Items", open the item's context menu, type the quantity into `InputNumeric`, close, quit â€” aborting as soon as the bags hold enough. It suppresses AutoRetainer for the duration (`AutoRetainer.SetSuppressed`), so the two do not fight over the bell. Also exposes `Blocker()` (a one-sentence, actionable reason a fetch cannot run: AllaganTools off, no bell in range, already busy), `Available(itemId)` (refreshes Artisan's `RetainerData` via `GetRetainerItemCount(id, tryCache:false)` â€” which is also what makes `RestockFromRetainers` able to do anything, since it returns immediately when that cache has no entry for the item), `Busy()` and `Abort()`.
- **Two new dispatch phases, `Retrieve` and `WaitRetrieve`, ahead of everything else** (`Adapters/DispatchService.cs`), so the order is now Retrieve â†’ ARC â†’ GBR â†’ Artisan. Per material: ask Artisan what it can actually see on the retainers, start the withdrawal, wait for its task queue to drain, then **measure the bag-count delta** â€” Artisan going idle is not proof anything moved, the same lesson as `WaitCraftEnd` in 0.1.1.0. A partial pull is expected, because `RestockFromRetainers` stops as soon as one retainer's pass satisfies its own bag check, so the remainder is re-queued, bounded at 4 attempts per item. A 4-minute watchdog aborts a stuck session and reports why.
- **Post-fetch re-plan** (`DispatchService.AfterRetrieve`) â€” once anything has actually landed in the bags, the cart is re-planned against the new inventory, so crafts that were deferred purely because their materials sat on a retainer become real crafts. This is the difference between `crafts finished 0/0, 4 still to retrieve` and `crafts finished 107/107`. Deferrals caused by a retrieval we are about to perform are no longer printed up front â€” the player is not told a craft is blocked and then told it ran; whatever is still stuck after the fetch is reported once, at the end.
- `DispatchService.RetrieveOne(itemId, quantity)` and `DispatchService.RetrieveOnly(retrievals)` â€” the fetch machinery without the crafting, for the tree button and `/lcraft fetch`.
- `Configuration.cs` â€” `RetrieveFromRetainers` (config v4), **ON by default**: an existing config that never had the field gets the new behaviour, because that is the fix that was asked for. It is opt-out, not opt-in.

- **Why this drives Artisan and not AutoRetainer, despite AutoRetainer being the card's first choice.** Read from the installed `AutoRetainer.dll` 4.6.1.34 with ILSpy 11.0.0.9375 â€” decompiled, not guessed from the string table. Its 27 IPC names are all venture / postprocess / multi-mode and none withdraws an item. The only reverse-direction code it has is `AutoRetainer.Scheduler.Tasks.TaskEntrustDuplicates.EnqueueNewReverse(EntrustPlan)`, public static, and it is the wrong shape three times over. (1) Its first queued step is literally *"Wait until addon SelectString ready"*: it assumes a retainer session is **already open**, and contains no bell interaction and no retainer selection, so it cannot start from a standing player. (2) It is driven by an `EntrustPlan` whose `EntrustItemsAmountToKeep` is an amount-to-keep-at-the-far-end, not an amount-to-fetch, and it moves whole slots via `MoveSlotFromToRetainerInventoryUnsafe` rather than a requested quantity. (3) `RetrieveFromRetainer` â€” the promising-looking name in the string table â€” is a literal of the `RetainerItemCommand` enum, not a callable. Passing the delta withdraws the delta and then stops, which is what we want, but it can also stop early after a partial pull â€” hence the measure-and-return loop rather than trusting the call.
- **A summoning bell is required, and only retainers are reachable.** The chocobo saddlebag, the armoury chest and the glamour dresser are not bell inventories, so stock sitting there is still named and refused â€” once, with the reason â€” rather than silently retried. Same for AllaganTools being absent (Artisan's retainer features are a no-op without it) and for the toggle being off. Every refusal now says what to do about it instead of repeating itself.
